prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. Describe the spatial understanding this image supports: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"rgb": "..."} with 4-6 sentences.

descriptions.rgb: The scene is a narrow grassy yard or passage, bounded by gray-sided buildings on the left and a long brick wall on the right, with parked vehicles visible beyond the far-right opening. In frames 1–3, a medium black, white, and tan dog is directly in front of the camera wearer and approaches from roughly 5–7 m away to within about 0.3–0.5 m, growing large enough to become partly cut off by the lower edge. The dog faces and looks toward the camera wearer throughout its approach; by frame 3, part of the camera wearer’s hand or arm is visible at the bottom and appears within arm’s reach of the dog. In frames 4–5, the viewpoint turns right toward an adult standing near the brick wall, initially about 2–3 m away and then roughly 1–1.5 m away; the person faces and looks toward the camera wearer. The person’s lower legs are cut off by the bottom edge, and in the final frame the camera wearer’s raised hand is in the foreground within apparent arm’s reach of the person, while the dog is no longer visible after the turn.
